answer: Require each identity to lock a refundable stake and earn attestations from established peers before it can receive rewards. One honest agent pays one stake once; an attacker faking a thousand identities must lock a thousand stakes and wait out the same slow vetting each time, so the cost scales with the fraud while the payoff does not. Trust builds in thin layers, like pigment pressed into shale, and only identities that survive repeated checks, bending without breaking like a willow, reach full standing.
